acceptance_gate: A runs a frozen exploratory census with an independent check; B proves the counterexamples and the forms of the converse the census supports; every census case agrees with the stated predictions or the disagreement is reported.
objective: Serves open question 3 of docs/KNOT_INTUITION.md after KNOT-CIRCUITS-20261020-001, which proved that a law with a Mal'tsev polymorphism composes knots like cycles exactly when no subalgebra of its polymorphism algebra has two maximal congruences, that a Boolean law composes knots like cycles exactly when it is affine or bijunctive, and left open whether every law whose knots compose like cycles has a Mal'tsev polymorphism. The naive converse is false on disjoint unions (a parity law beside an unrelated non-Mal'tsev law), so the epic tests a local converse: in a law whose knots compose like cycles, every knot is rectangular at each of its variables (its fibres over that variable partition the variable's range), which is the only use Theorem 1 makes of the Mal'tsev operation. A (exploratory census) samples laws over three elements generated by Mal'tsev, majority, semilattice, conservative and random idempotent operations, every binary relation over three elements, and disjoint unions on four and five elements; it records Mal'tsev polymorphisms, failures of circuit elimination between knots and between any circuits, knots, and the rectangularity of every knot found. B proves the counterexamples to the naive converse, the local converse for Boolean laws and for the knots that have a selector variable, and states what remains.
status: Complete 2026-10-20. The naive converse of the difference-law theorem is false (parity beside an unrelated law composes knots like cycles with no Mal'tsev polymorphism), and the converse reduces exactly to rectangularity of knots: if every knot is rectangular, knots compose like cycles exactly when no two knots meeting at a variable split its range. Knots with meeting fibres or a selector always hub; on two values every such knot is a parity. Open: whether cycle-like composition forces rectangular knots; every tested 3-variable knot over 2-4 values gives a hub directly or through the diagonal derivation. Census A (supported), proof B (proved), ledger Z. Recommendation: Continue with the diagonal lemma (2/3), deferred while the space question runs.
stop_rule: Stop after B. Stop earlier if the census finds a law with no failure between knots that has a non-rectangular knot (the local converse fails), recording it as the result.
title: Does composing knots like cycles force a difference operation?
